newsitem.title: UK: Tired FTSE 100 sags as market eases in weekend.
newsitem.headline: Tired FTSE 100 sags as market eases in weekend.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 eased from a record high, giving up a small part of budget week's near 200-point gain and still closely tracking index futures.
The FTSE fell 15.7 points to 4,816 by 1236 GMT with September contract futures 37 points lower at 3,839.
Earlier the index reached a new all-time peak of 4,879 as futures powered ahead amid a massive squeeze.
"The volatility of the last week has taken everyone by surprise," said Merrill Lynch UK equities strategist, Tim Huddart.
"We've had a good run this week and that's enough. So unless the people who pushed the market up this morning reappear we'll be trading quietly down to the weekend," said Huddart.
Dealers and strategists celebrated today's reduced volatility with the market notching up a mere 65-point range.

Much of today's movement, like Thursday's, stemmed from post-budget position-squaring as interest rate views changed and with the market still calculating the ramifications of scrapping dividend tax relief.
"It is difficult to tell how much of today's business was genuine trading and how much related to arbitrage positions in the derivatives," said Huddart.
Market talk suggested that several big brokerages faced large losses after Britain's finance minister, Gordon Brown, bowled a curved ball into City projections.
"It is a very, very confused marketplace. There are huge two way pulls. It is very difficult to read it," said Charterhouse chief economist, Richard Jeffrey.

"There's uncertainty over what the eventual technical impact of the budget will be on the market, whether there will be a move away from equities (due to the abolition of dividend tax relief) although it was helpful on the economic front," he said.

The market has interpreted Wednesday's maiden budget from the new Chancellor to mean a sharp hike in interest rates is imminent, but looked on the bright side and pushed ahead on hopes that any dampening of inflationary pressures would ultimately be good news.
Enthusiam was just a little more subdued today.
"It's a bit quieter today. The reaction to the budget is certainly cooler and people are looking ahead to the weekend for a quieter look at what it all means," said NatWest strategist, David McBain.
The broader FTSE index, the Mid Cap 250, was 20.5 points weaker at 4,454.7.
With Wall Street closed for the U.S. Independence Day holiday the market is seen tracking FTSE futures for the rest of the session.
The market repeated Thursday's sectoral pattern with gains for domestic issues, especially banks, and big losses for exporters on worries over sterling strength.
Alliance & Leicester rose 16-1/2p to 616p and Standard Chartered 7-1/2p to 993p with other banks stocks outperforming the weaker market.
Big exporters suffered for a second day as worries intensified over dented profits with sterling's continuing strength.
GKN fell 33-1/2p to 925-1/2p and TI Group 15-1/2p to 464p. --London newsroom, +44 171 54 7717
